key_insight: Self-powered microsystems are becoming feasible by combining diverse ambient energy harvesters with smarter power management and hybrid integration, but system-level bottlenecks still limit real-world autonomy.
engineering_relevance: The review is relevant for designing maintenance-free IoT, wearable, and cyber-physical devices that need reliable low-power energy supply without frequent battery replacement.
method: Compare major harvesting modalities: TENGs, piezoelectric/pyroelectric devices, indoor photovoltaics, and RF rectennas
Examine hybrid multi-source integration and impedance-matching strategies
Assess ultra-low-voltage cold-start PMICs and storage-device degradation under realistic conditions
evidence_signal: The abstract cites specific progress such as liquid-solid TENGs reducing wear, nonlinear piezoelectric oscillators broadening bandwidth by over 300%, and metamaterial-based RF harvesters enabling broadband operation.
watch_item: Hybrid energy systems can fail in practice if cold-start circuitry, source matching, and storage degradation are not addressed together.
paper_title: Energy Harvesting for Self-Powered Microsystems: A Critical Review of Materials, Power Management, and System Integration
